# Saltroad — Playtest Notes (Round 3 of 5)

> Synthetic public test fixture. Free-form feedback notes, not rules. Quotes are paraphrased and nothing here overrides the rulebook.

## Session overview

|  Session  |  Houses  |  Length  |  Tester notes                      |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
|  A        |  4       |  95 min  |  Auction felt tense, trade slow    |
|  B        |  3       |  70 min  |  Few bandits drawn                 |
|  C        |  5       |  120 min |  Too long; tolls felt fiddly       |
|  D        |  2       |  55 min  |  Ghost Wagon too easy to beat      |

## What testers liked

- The blind **permit auction** produced the loudest reactions of the night.
- Reading **Rumor** cards aloud made new players feel the world moving.
- Climbing a **Guild Rank** felt like a real reward, especially reaching Factor.

## What testers asked about

- "Does the **Toll** on a road segment apply if I stop in the middle of it?" The facilitator checked the table rule for the session but asked us to clarify the wording.
- "Can I use a **Guild Letter** against a toll or only against an embargo?" Three of five testers guessed wrong.
- "Is a **Standoff** worth two coin or one?" The reference card and the rule text disagreed in the old print.
- "Why would anyone ever buy a **Strongbox**?" Several testers read it as a trap; the designer wants it to be a hedge.

## Pace and length

- Session C ran twenty-five minutes over. The **Trade** step was the slowest part: five houses each buying and selling in turn.
- Idea: let houses declare their trades simultaneously. Concern: that removes the **permit order** advantage.
- Idea: shorten the Season from eight rounds to seven for five houses.

## Balance observations

|  Metric                      |  Target  |  Current       |  Notes                        |
| ---------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | ----------------------------- |
|  Houses finishing Bankrupt   |  ≤ 1     |  1.5           |  Wages feel steep early       |
|  Seals per house at the end  |  3 – 5   |  2.8           |  Seals too scarce             |
|  Royal Orders claimed        |  ≥ 5     |  3             |  Gullhaven too far to reach   |
|  Bandit encounters per game  |  4 – 8   |  5             |  OK                           |

## Wording to revisit

- The word "**settle**" is used for both contracts and bids; testers mixed them up.
- "Ledger" appears on both the round tracker and a step name; consider renaming one.
- The **Dust Season** dial lacks an example of what "apply every Rumor effect twice" means.

## Component notes

- The **Permit Tiles** are hard to tell apart in dim light; add numerals.
- **Embargo Discs** were mistaken for coins; make them a different color.
- Bid screens are tall enough to hide small coins, which testers liked.

## Next steps

- Reprint reference cards with the corrected **Standoff** amount.
- Test a Guild Seal reward for the first house to fulfill a **Royal Order**.
- Playtest the five-round Season with groups of two.

## Session logs

### Session A (four houses)

The Wren house won with a Fortune of 88, mostly from two Royal Orders delivered to Gullhaven in rounds six and seven. The Heron house went Bankrupt twice after buying an **Iron-rimmed Wheels** upgrade too early. Round five's **Bridge Out** Rumor made the Cinderford–Dunmarket segment so costly that nobody used it, and Dunmarket sat unvisited for the whole second half. Testers suggested the toll be lower or shorter in duration.

### Session B (three houses)

Quiet Roads came up twice, so only three Bandit cards were drawn in the whole game. The group felt the bandit rule barely mattered. Nobody had noticed what **Salt Lantern** does until reading the card.

### Session C (five houses)

The five-house game used the full map including Dunmarket and Fenmoor. The permit auction took nearly fifteen minutes in round one as everyone tried to guess bids. From round three onward bidding sped up. Players asked for an optional timer. The **Syndicate** module was tried for the first time: Wren and Heron formed one at round three and shared Seals, which made the Factor privilege arrive two rounds early. Other houses felt this was too strong.

### Session D (two houses)

The two-house map skips Brine Wells, Dunmarket, and Fenmoor, which testers liked for speed. The Ghost Wagon was beaten easily by a house that bought Salt in Ashgate and sold in Gullhaven every round. We will raise the Ghost Wagon's starting Coin.

| ------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------- |
|  Lower the Bridge Out toll from 3 to 2     |  Session A  |  Accepted     |
|  Add numerals to Permit Tiles              |  Session B  |  Accepted     |
|  Optional bid timer of 45 seconds          |  Session C  |  Under test   |
|  Syndicates only from five houses          |  Session C  |  Under test   |
|  Raise Ghost Wagon starting Coin to 60     |  Session D  |  Accepted     |
|  Rename one of the two uses of "Ledger"    |  Several    |  Open         |

## Tester quotes (paraphrased)

- "I never felt safe at the table. Someone always knew what I was carrying."
- "The Glut rule is clever. It made me sell Spice one round early."
- "I wanted more reasons to go back to Ashgate."
- "Bandits are fine, but I want an escort that is not just coins."

## Accessibility notes

- Dye (red) and Spice (orange) cubes are hard to tell apart for color-blind testers; add shapes.
- The Price Chart uses very small numerals; enlarge them.
- Text on Town cards is dense; consider icons for what each town buys.
